chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Florence Mills, Ziegfeld and the Harlem theatre scene
summary: At 14 to 16 she met Florence Mills through Jeanette. She relates Ziegfeld's way of handling singers, and describes Mills as sweet and delicate, like Josephine Baker.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Do you want to jump to Florence Mills?
Oh, yes. I met Florence Mills when I was about 14. By the way, I went home to look for some things and I
had some stockings that I wore during that period. I brought my dates up to where I knew what was happening if I had to tell the story. I found a picture of Jeanette -
Oh really? Of Seymour and Jeanette?
Yes. Florence Mills was a very good friend of Jeanette's. Jeanette used to take me everywhere with her. See I was very young and she wouldn't dare to leave me alone.

Between 14 and 16. I met Ziegfeld. Oh, a wonderful thing about Ziegfeld, I heard them talking in the dressing room that whenever he found a good singer like Sarah or Ella he'd really make a singer by introducing this singer to a very handsome, tall, handsome good-looking guy and the minute he felt that she was in love with this man, he'd snatch the man away from her. He'd say, "Now go out and sing!" She'd never see the man again. He'd say, "Now you'll sing with more feeling." He had his way of dealing with people to make them dance and sing. Florence Mills was the most beautiful little delicate-looking person and very sweet. I was wondering why there isn't more said or done about her because she was a great star. I met her. Met Gertrude Saunders, the girl that - I think they had difficulties out of Gertrude Saunders, so Ziegfeld found Florence Mills to take her place.
When you knew Florence Mills, what was she doing then?

She was in a show on - I think it was Seventh Avenue. You know the night clubs and theatres were a big thing. There was no Broadway then; it was Seventh Avenue and Harlem. Everything existed there, you know.
Tell me a little bit about Florence Mills. In performance, what was she like?
Just beautiful. She reminded me of - what was the girl from Paris? Josephine Baker, that type.
They were contemporaries, were'nt they, just about the same time?
